headline: Entry proof weather: the rate is visible, but proof capacity is the front to watch.
dek: W31 weather keeps policy, forced-labor proof, freight, import timing, apparel sourcing and input scarcity as separate stations. Do not blend them into a fake composite metric.

zones.name: Tariff authority
zones.operator_meaning: USTR announced final Section 301 action tied to forced-labor import enforcement against 60 economies, with 10% or 12.5% treatment, net-of-MFN handling for some partners and product exemptions.
zones.watch: USTR and Federal Register clarifications on country treatment, product exemptions and annex detail.

zones.name: Entry clock
zones.operator_meaning: The Federal Register notice made covered products entered or withdrawn for consumption on or after 12:01 a.m. ET on 24 July in scope, with relief for qualifying goods already loaded and in transit if entered before 12:01 a.m. ET on 28 July.
zones.watch: Broker instructions, vessel status, warehouse withdrawal timing and entry records.

zones.name: Forced-labor proof
zones.operator_meaning: Reuters reported the UFLPA Entity List expanded from 144 to 187 entities across sectors including pharmaceuticals, metals, cotton, food and lithium.
zones.watch: UFLPA list updates, detention data, sector alerts and supplier proof responsiveness.

zones.name: Freight station
zones.operator_meaning: Drewry's 30 July World Container Index fell 3% to $4,255 per 40-foot container, while lane rates remain a separate metric family from tariff treatment.
zones.watch: Drewry and Freightos lane movements, kept separate from import volume and compliance proof.

zones.name: Import calendar
zones.operator_meaning: NRF/Hackett forecast July covered-port imports at 2.47 million TEU and August at 2.22 million TEU, while Reuters/Descartes reported June U.S. container imports up 8.2% year over year.
zones.watch: Whether pull-forward creates entry congestion, inventory overhang or orderly August normalization.

zones.name: Apparel sourcing
zones.operator_meaning: The White House memo directs textile and apparel tariff-rate quota feasibility for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia by 1 September 2026; Reuters reported Vietnam faces a higher 12.5% rate than named peers.
zones.watch: Country placement, quota feasibility, cotton-input proof, supplier labor evidence and lead-time tradeoffs.

zones.name: Input scarcity
zones.operator_meaning: The current package keeps ISM supplier deliveries, prices and short-supply commodities as a separate reference station, with July ISM due after the W31 package.
zones.watch: The 3 August ISM manufacturing release for supplier deliveries, prices and short-supply commodities.

reference_cards.label: Import coverage claim
reference_cards.note: USTR fact sheet claim for affected trade partners; not a treatment decision.

reference_cards.label: Effective time
reference_cards.note: Federal Register clock for covered entries.

reference_cards.label: In-transit cutoff
reference_cards.note: Relief cutoff for qualifying goods already loaded and in transit.

reference_cards.label: UFLPA Entity List
reference_cards.note: Reuters reported expansion from 144 to 187 entities.

reference_cards.label: Drewry WCI
reference_cards.note: 30 July WCI composite, down 3%; keep separate from tariff proof.

operator_translation: Build an entry proof board with one row per shipment or SKU group: origin, HTS, authority, exemption status, in-transit status, supplier proof, broker instruction, landed-cost treatment, customer exposure, owner and next review time.
operator_watchlist: CBP/USTR implementation guidance and broker practice after the Federal Register notice.
UFLPA list updates, detention data and sector alerts.
Drewry and Freightos lane movement, kept as separate metric families.
NRF/Hackett August and September forecasts versus Reuters/Descartes reported TEUs.
Textile TRQ details for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia and Malaysia before or on 1 September.
ISM supplier deliveries, prices and short-supply commodities after the 3 August release.

newsletter_insert.title: Supply Chain Weather
newsletter_insert.headline: Entry proof weather: proof capacity is the front, not the rate table.
newsletter_insert.body: This week's weather map has separate stations for tariff authority, the 24-28 July entry clock, forced-labor proof, freight, import timing, apparel sourcing and input scarcity. They should not be blended into one risk number because each station has a different source, owner and clock.
newsletter_insert.operator_translation: Before the next entry or customer-pricing decision, open one entry proof board: product, origin, HTS, authority, exemption status, in-transit status, supplier proof, broker instruction, landed-cost treatment, customer exposure and named owner. External watch items stay external; internal rows get owners.
